hypothesis: A clearly mechanical one-time accounting loss that does not change cash obligations may be confused with deteriorating operating fundamentals; put richness is a separate pricing-stage gate.
amendment_log: Candidate-pool coverage expanded at coordinator request to include accounting_error_correction before reviewing that category. Economic rule unchanged; no price outcomes accessed.
positive_rule: The contemporaneous filing or exhibit identifies an actual or estimated noncash loss or charge, not a gain.

The filing identifies a mechanical accounting cause, such as an accounting-standard/technical tax remeasurement, pension actuarial remeasurement, or translation adjustment. Ordinary asset/goodwill write-downs, investment price declines and restructuring are not automatically mechanical.

There is affirmative contemporaneous evidence that this accounting adjustment creates no new cash obligation or affects neither cash flow nor cash obligations; the word noncash by itself is insufficient.

There is no explicit concurrent operating deterioration, guidance cut, default, loss of demand, business closure, failed project, or loss of expected future cash generation disclosed in the same filing/exhibit.

The full contemporaneous filing/exhibit must corroborate the supporting text. Unchanged operating outlook, where explicitly provided, is recorded as corroboration; silence does not establish an unchanged outlook.
Keep at most one event per issuer and filing date.
controls: Other auditable charge/loss events in the same categories, annotated with why the mechanical/no-new-cash rule fails. Gains, missing source text and ambiguous cases are unclassified rather than controls.
sources: Save source annotations and retrieval status, including mechanical cause, cash statement, operating-outlook statement and any negative evidence.
prohibited: No assuming noncash means economically harmless
No using future recovery or subsequent guidance to classify a prior charge
No loosening the rule to obtain trades
